cross_refs.citation: 42 U.S.C. § 3604 — Fair Housing Act § 3604 Prohibited Acts
cross_refs.relationship: concurrent claim — § 3604(b)/(f) discriminatory housing terms companion; where DV victim status intersects with protected class (sex, disability), both statutes apply
fraud instrument — false HUD Form 5382 self-certification to obtain federally funded housing = false claim; qui tam relator path available to person harmed by fraudulent DV claim

cross_refs.citation: 42 U.S.C. § 1983 — Civil Rights Act of 1871 — Government Actor Liability
cross_refs.relationship: enforcement companion — § 1983 reaches government actors (housing authorities, court officials) who administered a fraudulent DV-based housing placement; state action required

cross_refs.citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 — FEHA Housing Anti-Discrimination
cross_refs.relationship: state law parallel — where federal § 12491 program covers CA-based housing, CA FEHA § 12955 may run concurrently; broader protected classes under state law

cross_refs.citation: 18 U.S.C. § 1001 — False Statements to Federal Agencies
cross_refs.relationship: criminal exposure — knowing false statement on HUD Form 5382 to a federal housing authority = potential § 1001 violation; element: statement to department/agency of the United States

boundary_note: § 12491 covers housing program access and DV-based housing protections. The criminal DV case (PC § 273.5, PC § 243(e)), family court DVRO proceedings (FC § 6200 et seq.), and custody matters are owned by CA_Criminal_Law_Specialist and CA_Family_Law_Litigator respectively. The False Claims Act qui tam theory is owned by US_Federal_Financial_Fraud_Litigator. § 12491 provides the housing statute anchor; companion Citizens provide the fraud and enforcement layers.
